solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poisonous vapour causing drama with gusts swirling (10, two words)

indicators.note: things that swirl are churned about, so the letters before it are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
joins the two words of fodder

explanation.surface: A stage play whipped up by gusts of wind somehow releases a toxic cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: This chemical weapon of the First World War was a blistering poison released as a cloud over enemy trenches.

clue.text: Black music: mark query/answer dividing Indian city without lore

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: letters dividing a word split it apart by sitting in its middle
without means lacking, so the city's name loses the word that follows

parts.note: Bangalore, now Bengaluru, is in Karnataka
taken as written
Q is the abbreviation for query or question
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A note on a piece of township music queries its links to an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangalore, now officially Bengaluru, loses its last four letters, and the question-and-answer pair is wedged into what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Mbaqanga is a South African popular music style that grew up in the black townships around Johannesburg in the 1960s.

clue.text: Absorbing books I use variously, he works for main contractor

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the reworked word swallows the other pieces
variously means in different ways, so the letters of the short word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book, doubled for books
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tradesman takes in books and uses them as he likes while working for the main firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Subbie is British informal for subcontractor, common on building sites.
explanation.definitionFit: A subcontractor is hired by a main contractor to do part of the job, and subbie is its informal short form.

clue.text: Short pants, once straight?

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word that follows loses its last letter

parts.note: trews are close-fitting tartan trousers, and pants is the American word for trousers

explanation.surface: A pair of trousers that was once cut straight is now too short.
explanation.walkthrough: Trew is an old spelling of true, and true can mean straight, as in 'a true line'.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean exactly straight or aligned, and trew is an obsolete spelling of that word.

clue.text: Moving back, rediscovered sincere roots

indicators.note: rediscovered suggests uncovered afresh in a new form, so the letters are re-formed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Going home again, someone has rediscovered their true roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrocession is the act of going back or receding, and in law a ceding back of territory.

clue.text: A sink

parts.note: surface reading: a kitchen basin with a plughole; setter's reading: a sink in its older sense of a cesspit or privy

explanation.walkthrough: This was the Azed competition word, so the clue is a bare definition with no wordplay; solvers sent in their own clues for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught-house is an archaic biblical word for a privy or cesspool, the old sense of sink as a drain for filth.

clue.text: Remove from legacy, making one think

parts.note: a means one
to deem is to judge or think

explanation.surface: Being cut out of a will makes one stop and think.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to adeem is to revoke a bequest, for example because the item no longer exists in the estate.

clue.text: Minor joist needing to settle I instilled

indicators.note: something instilled is put inside, so the letter is set within the verb

parts.note: to solve a problem is to settle it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small roof beam needs fixing before I can put it in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A solive is a small secondary floor beam or joist resting on the main beams.

clue.text: Monster discovered in antenatal after being operated on

indicators.note: something operated on has been cut and rearranged, so the word's letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monstrous growth shows up on a prenatal scan and is then removed by surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monster' is an adjective-like noun here: Atlantean means gigantic, like Atlas, and as a noun a giant.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantean describes something huge and strong like the Titan Atlas, so a giant or monster fits.

clue.text: Dead removed from fortification found in ditch

indicators.note: removed from means taken out of, so the letter is dropped from the word that follows

parts.note: a redan is a V-shaped field fortification
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: Bodies are taken from a fort and found lying in a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rean, or reen, is a dialect word for a watercourse or drainage channel between fields.

clue.text: Group creating fuzzy impression from puff book left off

indicators.note: something left off is omitted, so the named letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a puff is a short promotional write-up on a book jacket
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A band whose sound is hazy, like a jacket write-up with the book itself missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions plus wordplay: Blur is the Britpop band, and a blur is also an indistinct shape; the wordplay drops the final B of BLURB.
explanation.definitionFit: Blur were a leading 1990s Britpop band, and a smudged indistinct appearance is a common noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Jewellers' stone presented by person that is including marriage portion

parts.note: per means for each person, as in a price per head

indicators.note: something including another holds it within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is
a dot is a dowry, from French

explanation.surface: A jeweller's gem is handed over by someone as part of a wedding dowry.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives this spelling as a variant of peridot; dot for a dowry comes from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gem variety of olivine, cut and set by jewellers; this is an alternative spelling.

clue.text: Playwright even if old-fashioned

definitions.note: the archaic sense is signalled by old-fashioned
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an archaic form of albeit

explanation.surface: A dramatist is acknowledged even though his style is dated.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Albee wrote Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?; Chambers lists albe or albee as an old form of albeit.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Albee was an American dramatist, and the same spelling is an obsolete conjunction meaning although.

clue.text: Scotsman's great, leading ace — some bloke

parts.note: in Scots, fell means very or great
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A Scotsman says it's great, with an ace leading, about some guy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' places FELL in front of A.
explanation.definitionFit: Fella is an informal spelling of fellow, a casual word for a man or chap.

clue.text: Water birds around shoal in large woody plants (9, two words)

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the birds wrap about the underwater feature

parts.note: terns are seabirds
a shoal is a shallow underwater bank, like a reef

explanation.surface: Seabirds circle a sandbank among big plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoal' tempts as a shoal of fish, which suits seabirds, but here it is the shallow bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree ferns are tall tropical ferns with a woody trunk-like stem, so large woody plants describes them.

clue.text: Malay travel that is returning during prohibition

indicators.note: something during another happens within its span, so these pieces go inside the outer word

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is
to run is to travel, as a bus runs

explanation.surface: A Malaysian traveller doubles back during a time of prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the abbreviation for 'that is' is turned round; the travel word stays forwards before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a Malay sultanate on Borneo, so a citizen of it is Malay by language and culture.

clue.text: Noble, one leading unruly riots

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: something unruly will not keep order, so the letters of the next word are disorderly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman is at the head of disorderly street riots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' puts A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristo is informal shorthand for aristocrat, a person of titled or high-born rank.

clue.text: Bird losing head in lift?

indicators.note: losing its head means the word's first letter is cut off

parts.note: to lift something is to steal it

explanation.surface: A bird loses its head in an elevator, the question mark admitting the oddity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like an elevator, but it is the slang verb for pinching.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Jumpers execute this early — they start with one

indicators.note: each of the words before the dash starts with one letter, and only those openings are taken

parts.note: opening letter
opening letter
opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: Leapers perform this move at the start of a routine, and a jump starts on one foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumpers are ballet dancers; 'they start with one' also hints that a jeté takes off from one foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeté is a ballet leap from one foot to the other, so dancers who jump perform it.

clue.text: Part of ship's side left full of brine rising

indicators.note: something full of another has it inside, so the side word wraps the brine word

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: brine is salt water

explanation.surface: Part of a ship's left side is soaked as the salt sea rises.
explanation.walkthrough: Left as port is the standard nautical convention, facing the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: The portlast is the gunwale, the upper edge of a ship's side, an old nautical term.

clue.text: Ecstasy experienced returning? This calls for blessing

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so everything before it is read right to left

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
something seen has been experienced, as in 'seen it all'

explanation.surface: A drug trip is relived and someone asks for a blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: Neese is an old spelling of sneeze, which by custom prompts 'bless you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneeze traditionally draws the response 'bless you', so this cryptic description fits the obsolete word.

clue.text: Brother Etonian must forgo outside foursomes for this

indicators.note: forgoing the outer groups of four means the four letters at each end are given up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Old Etonian has to skip the golf foursomes on this occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Run the two words together and strip BROT from the front and NIAN from the back. Foursomes suggests golf, but it means groups of four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereto is a formal adverb meaning to this or for this purpose, found in legal documents.

clue.text: Heroine, divine lady outwardly, displaying budding protuberances

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the goddess surrounds the heroine

parts.note: Ge or Gaia is the Greek earth goddess
Emma is the title heroine of Jane Austen's novel

explanation.surface: A heroine and a goddess show off their blossoming figures.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany and zoology these are small bud-like outgrowths that detach to grow into new organisms.

clue.text: Miss being parched inside? Spirits required

indicators.note: inside places the dry word within the title

parts.note: Ms is the title for a woman
arid means parched

explanation.surface: A thirsty young woman needs a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' suggests drink to the thirsty lady, but they are jinn.
explanation.definitionFit: Marids are powerful jinn in Arabian mythology, so they are supernatural beings or spirits.

clue.text: Wander about in Scotland, having time to vouch

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to aver is to state as true, to vouch for

explanation.surface: Someone roams Scotland and has the leisure to testify.
explanation.definitionFit: Taver is a Scots dialect verb for roaming aimlessly or rambling, recorded in Chambers.

clue.text: Vessel in line filling rendezvous

indicators.note: something filling another occupies its inside, so the letter goes within the meeting place

parts.note: a venue is a meeting place
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A ship joins the queue to reach the meeting point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A venule is a small vein carrying blood from the capillaries, so a tiny blood vessel.

clue.text: Dram suggests this dish

parts.note: surface reading: a tot of whisky calls to mind a particular food; setter's reading: the answer, taken as an instruction in a down entry, spells a word for a dram

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as PIN written upwards, which gives NIP, a dram. A dish is an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is slang for a good-looking person, and a pin-up is a glamorous person whose picture is pinned on a wall.

clue.text: Effect of sun, absorbing ray by reason of this

indicators.note: something absorbing another takes it in, so the note sits inside the warmth word

parts.note: the sun produces heat
ray or re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Sunshine takes in a ray of light, and that is the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' looks like a sunbeam, which suits the surface, but it is the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereat is a formal adverb meaning because of this or at this point.

clue.text: Urchin is second caught by wader

indicators.note: something caught by another is held in its grasp, so these pieces go inside the bird

parts.note: a heron is a wading bird
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A street urchin is promptly grabbed by a wading bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Urchin's older sense is a hedgehog; hérisson is French for hedgehog, and in Chambers it is a spiked barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Urchin is an old word for hedgehog, which is what the French borrowing herisson literally means.

clue.text: Cry of derision unreservedly follows end of match

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of match
out can mean openly, without reserve, as in 'say it out'

explanation.surface: Jeering breaks out openly when a game finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' puts OUT after H. Hout is a variant of hoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoot is a jeering shout of scorn, and hout is a recorded variant spelling of it.

clue.text: Fossil-bearing, revealing hybrid type of cattle I see

parts.note: a zo or dzo is a cross between a yak and a cow
taken as written
the letter C is pronounced like see

explanation.surface: A fossil site turns up a crossbred cow, I notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoic means relating to animals, and of rocks, containing fossil remains of animal life.

clue.text: It may seal oil, being a turn-off (not the first)

indicators.note: 'not the first' means its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: something boring is a turn-off

explanation.surface: A seal that stops oil leaking is a dull subject.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rubber ring of circular cross-section fitted into a groove to make a leak-proof seal in machinery.

clue.text: Cereal crop determined acreage

parts.note: dour can mean stubborn or determined
A is the abbreviation for acre or acreage

explanation.surface: A grain is grown across a resolutely farmed area of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Doura is a variant of durra, a sorghum grain grown for food in Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Waving, inappropriate when former reputation's involved

indicators.note: something involved is wrapped up within another, so the old word is set inside

parts.note: undue means unwarranted or inappropriate
los is an obsolete word for praise or renown

explanation.surface: Someone acts improperly when their past reputation comes into it.
explanation.walkthrough: Los is a Spenserian word for praise or fame, which is why the clue calls it former.
explanation.definitionFit: Undulose describes something with a wavy, rippling outline, the botanical sense of undulating.

clue.text: Lines dividing island indicating disasters?

indicators.note: lines dividing a thing cut through its middle, so they sit inside it

parts.note: IS is the map abbreviation for island
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Boundary lines cutting through an island hint at calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills are misfortunes or troubles, so calamities fit; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Prickly trees surrounded by fragrance

indicators.note: something surrounded by another is enclosed in it, so the trees go inside the smell

parts.note: a scent is a fragrance
pines are conifers

explanation.surface: Spiky conifers give off a pleasant woody smell.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany spinescent means bearing spines or tapering to a spine, so it is spiny and sharp.
